activities.title: Who is still on the branch
activities.intro: Story time. In a take-away story some things go away, and then we count who is left. Listen to the story, touch each one as you count, then tap how many are left.
activities.offScreen: Go line up five toys, fly two of them away to another room, and count who is left for a grown-up.

rounds.prompt: Five birds sat on the branch. Two of them flew away. These are the birds still on the branch. Tap how many are left.
Six leaves were on the tree. Two blew away in the wind. These are the leaves still on the tree. Tap how many are left.
Three cups were on the table. One went to the sink. These are the cups still on the table. Tap how many are left.
Five stones sat in a row on the path. Four of them rolled into the pond. The flower was always there, just watching. Tap how many stones are left.

activities.title: Flew away or stayed
activities.intro: In these stories some things go and some things stay. Make two piles: the ones that went away, and the ones that stayed.
activities.offScreen: Ask a grown-up for a going-away story, then act it with your toys and make two piles.

rounds.prompt: The red birds flew away and the blue birds stayed on the branch. Put the birds that flew away in one pile and the birds that stayed in the other pile, then count each pile out loud.
The yellow leaves blew away and the green leaves stayed on the tree. Put the leaves that blew away in one pile and the leaves that stayed in the other pile, then count each pile out loud.
The little fish swam away down the stream and the big fish stayed in the pond. Put the fish that swam away in one pile and the fish that stayed in the other pile, then count each pile out loud.
The stones rolled away into the pond and the blocks stayed on the path. Put the ones that rolled away in one pile and the ones that stayed in the other pile, then count each pile out loud.

activities.title: Cover them up, then count
activities.intro: Now everybody is still here at the start. Listen for how many go away, cover those ones with your hand so they are gone, and then tap how many are left.
activities.offScreen: Build a tower of six blocks, knock two off, and tell a grown-up how many are still standing.

rounds.prompt: Five birds are on the branch. Two of them fly away. Cover two birds with your fingers so they are gone, then tap how many are left.
Six leaves are on the tree. One blows away. Cover one leaf with your finger so it is gone, then tap how many are left.
Six blocks are on the floor. Two go into the box. Cover two blocks with your fingers so they are gone, then tap how many are left.
Five fish are in the pond. Four of them swim away. Cover four fish with your hand so they are gone, then tap how many are left.

parentCard.title: The bird story you can cut out
steps: Sit down together with paper and crayons and draw one long branch across the page. Ask them how many birds should sit on it, and settle on five.
Draw the five birds together, one at a time, counting out loud as each one lands: one, two, three, four, five.
Cut the birds out. A grown-up holds the scissors if the cutting is tricky, and they do the choosing and the peeling off.
Tell the story slowly: five birds sat on the branch, and two of them flew away. Let them fly two birds off the page with their own hand and land them somewhere else in the room.
Ask the question every single time: how many birds are left on the branch? Let them touch each one as they count. Then bring the birds back and tell it again with a different number flying away.
notice: Do they count the birds still on the branch, or do they try to remember a number from the last telling?
Can they tell the story back themselves, with the flying away in the right place?
Which do they like more, flying the birds away or counting who is left?
